questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in your lane?

options.text: Always stay away from the left side of the lane.
Always stay away from the right side of the lane.
Always stay away from the center of the lane.
Use whatever part of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whatever part of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: Why should you place a load low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
It may be hard to see over a high load.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A load placed too high on a motorcycle raises the center of gravity and can make the motorcycle unstable.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. What should you do?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.
Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright clothing every time you ride to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: At what point does alcohol start to impair your riding?
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking alcohol. Impairment begins well below the legal limit.

questions.question: What should a passenger do when riding with you?

options.text: Lean with you as you lean.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with you as you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with you. They should sit as far forward as comfortable and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.explanation: At night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlight when not following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: A left arm extended straight out means you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: After entering a turn, what should you do with the throttle?

options.text: Maintain steady speed or accelerate slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain steady speed or accelerate slowly.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through the turn to stabilize the suspension. Keep a steady speed or accelerate slowly.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may miss a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in a blind spot. The driver may move into your lane without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn:

options.text: Usually cannot be heard by others.

questions.explanation: A horn can help you get someone's attention quickly. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn. Other drivers may not hear it. Do not rely only on your horn to avoid danger.

questions.question: Which provides the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Which protects your eyes from wind the best?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not.

questions.question: If rain starts while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil deposits that are slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to be more visible.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up only increases danger.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Change power suddenly in a turn.
Ride the brake throughout the turn.

questions.explanation: Change gears before entering a turn, not during it.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, use both brakes:

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Use both front and rear brakes every time you slow or stop. This gives you maximum stopping power.

questions.question: How do most headache, cold, and hay fever medications affect you?

options.text: They make it hard to concentrate.

questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, and stress can make you drowsy. This can harm your ability to ride safely. Always know how a medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: To see better when passing a vehicle on its left, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see ahead better and makes oncoming traffic see you more easily.

questions.question: What reduces the effects of alcohol after drinking?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects on your body.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you need to slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you need to slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle brake light is smaller and less visible than a car's brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers notice when you slow down suddenly.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front or rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them together at the same time.
